environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 8.0 API deployed behind an NGINX Ingress Controller (v1.9.4) in a Kubernetes cluster with a custom ingress annotation `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: on` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret: infra/client-ca-bundle`. The client CA bundle contains only certificates issued by an internal PKI (HashiCorp Vault PKI engine, role restricted to `ou=workflow-agents`). The ingress terminates mTLS and only forwards requests that present a valid client certificate chaining to the internal CA. Additionally, the ingress sets `X-Client-Cert-DN` header and a NetworkPolicy restricts pod ingress to only the ingress controller CIDR. However, the application code itself does NOT validate the X-Client-Cert-DN header — the protection relies entirely on the ingress refusing to proxy unauthenticated connections.

config.network_policy: pod ingress limited to ingress-controller namespace CIDR 10.2.0.0/16
config.application_auth: none (no middleware, no header validation in code)
config.note: The application itself performs no authentication; ingress-level mTLS is the sole access control
